loop.text: Most data scientist loops run four kinds of round. Probability and statistics questions. A modeling case: how would you predict this? An experiment to design, usually an A B test. And a coding screen, in Python and pandas or in SQL.
loop.spoken: Most data scientist loops run four kinds of round. Probability and statistics questions. A modeling case: how would you predict this? An experiment to design, usually an A B test. And a coding screen, in Python and pandas or in sequel.

probe.text: Across the loop, interviewers probe five things.

ai.text: AI has brought in new questions.

series.text: The series runs in the track's order: eleven videos, from statistics to LLM evaluation, and a hundred and fifty-eight questions. Machine learning and experimentation each get two videos. In every one, the questions worth a figure come first, and the one-line answers close it.

practice.text: Each page carries practice too. Every one has concept checks, four add challenges that run in your browser, and a bank of a hundred and ten multiple-choice questions covers the whole track.

next.text: The track opens with statistics and probability, and so does this series. Next: Statistics.

probe-list.text: Statistics and probability: distributions, tests and intervals. Modeling: the bias and variance trade-off, regularization, validation, and the metric you pick. Experimentation: the design, its power, and the pitfalls. Coding, in pandas, NumPy and SQL. And communication: explaining a model and its caveats to someone who doesn't build them.
probe-list.spoken: Statistics and probability: distributions, tests and intervals. Modeling: the bias and variance trade-off, regularization, validation, and the metric you pick. Experimentation: the design, its power, and the pitfalls. Coding, in pandas, NumPy and sequel. And communication: explaining a model and its caveats to someone who doesn't build them.

ai-exp.text: Experiments on AI features, where the output changes from one run to the next, and the provider can change the model in the middle of a test.

ai-check.text: Checking code or an analysis an assistant wrote.

ai-rounds.text: And some coding rounds allow an assistant and grade how you check its work. Others ban it, so ask the recruiter about each round.

ai-eval.text: Evaluating a feature built on an LLM is now treated as a measurement problem: an eval set of test prompts, a confidence interval on the share of them it passes, and a check that an LLM judge, a model grading the answers, agrees with human experts.
